description: The Order of Reading the Psalms appoints the Psalter through once a month; the Lectionary appoints proper Psalms for Sundays and Feast Days
name: Psalter

options.label: Appointed
options.description: Proper Psalms where the Lectionary appoints them, with the monthly Psalter supplying ordinary days

options.label: Monthly Psalter
options.description: Always the Psalms for this day of the thirty-day Psalter, divided between the Offices

description: The book notes that the Psalter follows the translation of the great English Bible; other readings keep the selected Bible version
name: Psalter Translation

options.label: Coverdale Psalter
options.description: The Psalter as printed in the Prayer Book Tradition

options.label: Selected Bible version
options.description: Use the Bible version selected for the Daily Office

description: The rubric allows the Nicene Creed instead of the Apostles' Creed
name: Creed

options.label: Apostles' Creed
options.description: The Creed appointed at Mattins and Evensong

options.label: Nicene Creed
options.description: Permitted in place of the Apostles' Creed

description: The Dominus vobiscum is used by a Minister in Major Orders; otherwise the second form is said
name: Salutation

options.label: The Lord be with you
options.description: For a Minister in Major Orders

options.label: O Lord, hear our prayer
options.description: For a Minister not in Major Orders

description: Choose which group of Sentences of Scripture to open with
name: Opening Sentences

options.label: Seasonal
options.description: Use the Sentences appointed for the season or Feast Day

options.label: General
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "General"

options.label: Morning
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Morning"

options.label: Evening
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Evening"

options.label: Advent
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Advent"

options.label: Christmastide
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Christmastide"

options.label: Epiphanytide
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Epiphanytide"

options.label: Septuagesimatide
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Septuagesimatide"

options.label: Lent
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Lent"

options.label: Passiontide
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Passiontide"

options.label: Eastertide
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Eastertide"

options.label: Ascensiontide
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Ascensiontide"

options.label: Whitsuntide
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Whitsuntide"

options.label: Trinity Sunday
options.description: Always use the Sentences printed under "Trinity Sunday"

description: The book prints a longer and a shorter exhortation, and permits a single bidding in place of either
name: Exhortation to Penitence

options.label: Longer form
options.description: Dearly beloved brethren, the Scripture moveth us…

options.label: Shorter form
options.description: Beloved, we are come together in the presence of Almighty God…

options.label: Bidding only
options.description: Let us humbly confess our sins unto Almighty God

description: Which form of the Absolution is pronounced
name: Absolution

options.label: Declaration
options.description: Almighty God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ…

options.label: Short form
options.description: The Almighty and merciful Lord grant you Absolution…

options.label: No Priest present
options.description: Grant, we beseech thee, merciful Lord…

description: The rubric permits passing at once from the Sentences to the Lord's Prayer and Angelic Salutation, save on a Day of Fasting or Abstinence, when it is said whatever is chosen here
name: Penitential Opening

options.label: Full form
options.description: Exhortation, Confession, and Absolution

options.label: Omit
options.description: Pass from the Sentences to the Lord's Prayer and Angelic Salutation, except on a Day of Fasting or Abstinence

description: The rubric appoints the Antiphon before and after the Venite on the days named
name: Invitatory Antiphon

options.label: As appointed
options.description: Say the Antiphon on the days for which one is appointed

options.label: Omit
options.description: Say the Venite without an Antiphon

description: The Te Deum is appointed on Sundays and Festivals, the Benedicite on penitential Sundays and lesser days; the Old Testament Canticle may be said instead of either
name: Canticle after the First Lesson

options.label: As appointed
options.description: Te Deum or Benedicite, according to the day

options.label: Te Deum
options.description: Always the Te Deum laudamus

options.label: Benedicite
options.description: Always the Benedicite, omnia opera Domini

options.label: Old Testament Canticle
options.description: The daily Old Testament Canticle, permitted in place of either Hymn

description: The Minister may end Morning Prayer with such intercessions as he shall think fit, or with the Grace
name: After the Third Collect

options.label: All the Prayers
options.description: The Prayers and Thanksgivings printed after the Third Collect

options.label: The Grace only
options.description: End with the Grace

description: The Suffrages are said, kneeling, on all Ferias outside of Eastertide
name: Suffrages

options.label: As appointed
options.description: Say the Suffrages on Ferias outside Eastertide

options.label: Always
options.description: Always say the Suffrages

options.label: Omit
options.description: Never say the Suffrages

description: The Pretiosa is a laudable custom and may be added to Prime, after the Martyrology reading for the day
name: The Pretiosa at Prime

description: The Gloria in excelsis may be said instead of the Gloria Patri at the end of the last Psalm, except in Advent, Septuagesimatide, and Lent
name: Gloria at the last Psalm

options.label: Gloria Patri
options.description: Always the Gloria Patri

options.label: Gloria in excelsis
options.description: The Gloria in excelsis where the rubric allows it

description: In places where it may be convenient, the Marian Anthem follows the Conclusion
name: Marian Anthem

description: The Minister may end Evening Prayer with such Prayers as he shall think fit
name: After the Third Collect

options.label: All the Prayers
options.description: The Prayers and Thanksgivings printed after the Third Collect

options.label: The Grace only
options.description: End with the Grace

description: The book appoints a hymn for Ferial days, for Feast Days and Sundays, for Lent, and for Eastertide
name: Office Hymn

options.label: As appointed
options.description: The hymn appointed for the day and season

options.label: Te lucis ante terminum
options.description: Always the Ferial hymn

options.label: Salvator mundi Domine
options.description: Always the hymn for Feast Days and Sundays

description: The book prints two Collects at Compline
name: The Collect

options.label: Visit, we beseech thee
options.description: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this place…

options.label: Lord Jesu Christ
options.description: Lord Jesu Christ, Son of the living God…

description: The appropriate Marian Anthem is said or sung after the Conclusion
name: Marian Anthem
